            raise ValueError("Superuser must be assigned to is_staff=True.")
        if other_fields.get("is_superuser") is not True:
            raise ValueError("Superuser must be assigned to is_superuser=True.")
        return self.create_user(email, password, **other_fields)

# Codebase Report: Django + HTMX RealWorld (Conduit) — Notifications Feature Prep

## 1. Directory / App Layout

- **Project root**: `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1`
- **Config package**: `config/` — `settings.py`, `urls.py` (root URLconf), `wsgi.py`, `asgi.py`
- **Apps** live under `apps/` (each has `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`, `admin.py`, `apps.py`, `forms.py` where relevant, `migrations/`):
  - `apps/accounts` — custom User model, auth, profiles, follow
  - `apps/articles` — Article model, feed/detail/CRUD, favorite
  - `apps/comments` — Comment model, comment create/delete
- **Shared helpers**: `helpers/` — `context_processors.py`, `htmx.py`, `exceptions.py`, `tests.py`
- **Templates**: single top-level `templates/` dir (NOT per-app). `TEMPLATES DIRS = [BASE_DIR / "templates"]` with `APP_DIRS: True` also on. Subdirs: `templates/accounts/`, `templates/articles/`, `templates/partials/`, plus `templates/base.html`.
- **Static**: `static/` (STATICFILES_DIRS).
- **E2E tests**: `realworld/specs/e2e/` (Playwright, TypeScript). Playwright config at `playwright/playwright.config.ts`.
- Important: `config/settings.py` line 16 does `sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR / "apps"))`, so apps are importable both as `apps.accounts` (INSTALLED_APPS) AND directly as `accounts`/`articles`/`comments` (used throughout imports, e.g. `from articles.models import Article`). A new notifications app should be added to `INSTALLED_APPS` as `apps.notifications` and can be imported as `notifications`.

## 2. Models

### User — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/accounts/models.py`
Custom `AbstractUser` (email is `USERNAME_FIELD`, `username` separate unique CharField). Key line:
```python
class User(AbstractUser):
    email = models.EmailField("Email Address", unique=True)
    username = models.CharField(max_length=60, unique=True)
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)
    image = models.URLField(null=True, blank=True)
    followers = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False)
    ...
    def is_following(self, other_user) -> bool:
        return other_user.followers.filter(pk=self.id).exists() if self.is_authenticated else False
```
There is **no separate Profile model** — profile data lives on User. `AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"`.

**Follow semantics (important for notifications)**: `followers` is a non-symmetrical M2M on self. `profile_user.followers.add(request.user)` means "request.user now follows profile_user". So `user.followers.all()` = people who follow `user`; `User.objects.filter(followers=request.user)` = users that request.user follows (see articles feed view).

### Article — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/articles/models.py`
```python
class Article(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = ... (unique)
    summary = ...; content = ...
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated = ...
    tags = TaggableManager(blank=True)   # django-taggit
    favorites = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="favorites")
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True, max_length=255)
    objects = ArticleManager()  # custom queryset with .with_favorites(user)
```
`ArticleQuerySet.with_favorites(user)` annotates `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug auto-generated from title on first save.

### Comment — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/comments/models.py`
```python
class Comment(models.Model):
    article = models.ForeignKey(Article, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    content = models.TextField()
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated = ...
```
Accessed via `article.comment_set` (default reverse manager).

## 3. Follow / Favorite / Comment view implementations

All are **function-based**, decorated `@login_required` + `@require_POST`, and return an HTMX partial when `is_htmx(request)` else redirect.

### Follow/Unfollow — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/accounts/views.py` (`follow_view`, lines 129-151)
```python
@login_required
@require_POST
def follow_view(request, username):
    profile_user = get_object_or_404(User, username=username)
    if profile_user != request.user:
        if profile_user.followers.filter(pk=request.user.id).exists():
            profile_user.followers.remove(request.user)
            is_following = False
        else:
            profile_user.followers.add(request.user)   # <-- follow happens here
            is_following = True
    else:
        is_following = False
    if is_htmx(request):
        return render(request, "partials/follow_button.html",
                      {"profile_user": profile_user, "is_following": is_following})
    return redirect("profile", username=username)
```
Notification hook point: the `else` branch where a new follow is created.

### Favorite/Unfavorite — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/articles/views.py` (`article_favorite_view`, lines 151-162)
```python
@login_required
@require_POST
def article_favorite_view(request, slug):
    article = get_object_or_404(Article, slug=slug)
    if article.favorites.filter(id=request.user.id).exists():
        article.favorites.remove(request.user)
    else:
        article.favorites.add(request.user)   # <-- favorite happens here
    article = Article.objects.with_favorites(request.user).select_related("author").get(pk=article.pk)
    if is_htmx(request):
        return render(request, "partials/favorite_button.html", {"article": article})
    return redirect("article_detail", slug=slug)
```
Notification hook point: the `else` (add) branch; notify `article.author` (guard against self-favorite — currently self-favorite is allowed by the view).

### Comment creation — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/apps/comments/views.py` (`comment_create_view`, lines 11-21)
```python
@login_required
@require_POST
def comment_create_view(request, slug):
    article = get_object_or_404(Article, slug=slug)
    body = request.POST.get("body", "").strip()
    if body:
        Comment.objects.create(article=article, author=request.user, content=body)   # <-- notify article.author
    if is_htmx(request):
        comments = article.comment_set.select_related("author").order_by("-created")
        return render(request, "partials/comment_list.html", {"comments": comments, "article": article})
    return redirect("article_detail", slug=slug)
```

## 4. Navigation rendering & where to surface unread count

- **Base template**: `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/templates/base.html` — includes `partials/header.html` (navbar) and `partials/footer.html`. Loads HTMX 2.0.4; body has `hx-headers` with CSRF token.
- **Navbar**: `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/templates/partials/header.html`. Authenticated nav items: Home, New Article, Settings, and the user profile link. This is the idiomatic place to add a "Notifications" nav item with an unread badge. Active-state pattern uses `request.resolver_match.url_name`.
- **Context processor**: `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/helpers/context_processors.py` — `conduit_context(request)` registered in `settings.py` TEMPLATES OPTIONS (line 69). It already branches on `request.user.is_authenticated`. This is the natural place to add an `unread_notifications_count` to make the badge available on every page globally. Alternatively add a new context processor in `helpers/` and register it in the same list.

There is **no middleware** beyond Django defaults (settings.py lines 46-54) — no custom middleware. Per-user template data comes exclusively from the context processor above plus Django's auth context processor (`user` in templates).

## 5. URL routing & view conventions

- Root URLconf `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/config/urls.py` includes each app's `urls.py` at `""`: `include("articles.urls")`, `include("accounts.urls")`, `include("comments.urls")`. A notifications app would be added the same way: `path("", include("notifications.urls"))`.

## 6. Template organization & naming

- Full-page templates under per-feature subdirs: `templates/accounts/*.html`, `templates/articles/*.html`. They `{% extends "base.html" %}` and fill `{% block content %}`.
- Reusable/HTMX fragments in `templates/partials/`: `follow_button.html`, `favorite_button.html`, `comment_list.html`, `feed_content.html`, `article_list.html`, `article_meta.html`, `header.html`, `footer.html`. For a notifications feature, follow this: a full page `templates/notifications/list.html` plus a `templates/partials/` fragment for HTMX-driven updates (e.g. mark-as-read).

Each app has `migrations/`. Latest per app:
- `accounts`: **0003** (`0003_alter_user_username.py`) — after 0001_initial, 0002_rename_name_user_username
- `articles`: **0003** (`0003_alter_article_created.py`)

A new `notifications` app starts at `0001_initial`. Migrations are standard Django-generated (`python manage.py makemigrations`). In-memory SQLite is used for tests/e2e; migrations run via `call_command('migrate')` at server start (see playwright config).

- Only `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-a-1/helpers/tests.py` exists (tests `clean_integrity_error`). Per the docstring and `CLAUDE.md`, unit coverage is intentionally minimal — "e2e is the real test suite." Uses plain `unittest.TestCase`.
